title: CMake, ABIs, Native Memory, and Rust Interoperability

scout.purpose: Master cmake, abis, native memory, and rust interoperability through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend cmake, abis, native memory, and rust interoperability.

blocks.text: The NDK cross-compiles native libraries for specific Android ABIs and API levels. CMake with the NDK toolchain models targets, include paths, compile definitions, dependencies, visibility, and linking; build once per ABI in isolated directories. minSdk limits available native APIs. Prefer target-scoped configuration and one shared libc++ runtime when multiple shared libraries interact. Export only intended symbols and avoid C++ ABI contracts across independently built components unless toolchain compatibility is controlled.

blocks.text: Native memory requires explicit ownership through RAII in C++, lifetimes in Rust, or documented C handles. Rust can eliminate many memory-safety bugs but unsafe FFI, raw pointers, callbacks, allocator boundaries, panics, and C ABI design remain review points. Expose a small stable C ABI between Rust and JNI or C++ where practical. Never allocate in one runtime and free in another without a declared allocator contract. Account for alignment, width, endianness, struct layout, and nullable handles.

blocks.text: Build and test every shipped ABI on devices or representative emulators, inspect ELF dependencies and symbols, and verify App Bundle delivery. Use warnings as errors selectively, reproducible NDK/CMake versions, dependency provenance, hardening flags, and license evidence. Run sanitizers, fuzzers, stress, and cross-language lifetime tests. Measure whether native code provides a real portability or performance benefit after JNI and maintenance cost. Keep a managed fallback when product requirements allow.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

blocks.title: Expert trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Passing a Rust-owned allocation to C++ free or a C++ allocation to Rust deallocation crosses allocator contracts and can corrupt memory.

trap_check.mistake: Passing a Rust-owned allocation to C++ free or a C++ allocation to Rust deallocation crosses allocator contracts and can corrupt memory.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Build a Kotlin-JNI-C ABI-Rust pipeline for two ABIs with explicit ownership, hidden symbols, hardening, tests, fuzzing, and artifact inspection.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: Why prefer a C ABI at a Rust interoperability boundary?
recall.answer: It provides a smaller, more stable and language-neutral calling contract than compiler-specific C++ ABI details.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
